Content:
Suppose we want to find all of the solutions to the equation

Content:
[MATH: 0 ≤ x < 2π.]

Content:
To calculate a solution, we can reduce the equation to a more convenient form by dividing through by [MATH: \cos x,] and then use the identity [MATH: \tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}] to simplify. This gives
[MATH: \sin x − sqrt(3)\cos x|= 0; (\sin x)/(\cos x) − (sqrt(3)\cos x)/(\cos x)|= 0; (\sin x)/(\cos x) − (sqrt(3)\cos x)/(\cos x)|= 0; (\sin x)/(\cos x) − sqrt(3)|= 0; \tan x − sqrt(3)|= 0.]

Content:
Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate [MATH: \tan x\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \tan x = \sqrt{3}]

Content:
We can immediately calculate the principal value [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: x = \arctan(\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}]

Content:
Since [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{3}] lies inside the given domain, our first solution is [MATH: x_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{3}.]

Content:
To find the other solution in the given interval, we add [MATH: \pi\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: x_{2}|= x_{1} + π; = (π)/(3) + π; = (4π)/(3)]

Content:
So the solutions are [MATH: x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}.]

Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate [MATH: \tan x\mathbin{:}] [MATH: \tan x = -\dfrac{7}{5}]

The length of the interval for [MATH: x] is [MATH: 2\pi], so we will likely require [MATH: 2] solutions.

We can immediately calculate the principal value [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: x = \arctan\left(-\dfrac{7}{5}\right) \approx -54.46]

This value is outside the domain [MATH: 0^\circ \leq x < 360^\circ.] To get a value that's inside the domain, we add [MATH: 180^\circ\mathbin{:}] [MATH: x_{1}|= \arctan (− (7)/(5)) + 180^{∘}; ≈ − 54.46^{∘} + 180^{∘}; = 125.54^{∘}]

To find the other solution inside the given interval, we add [MATH: 180^\circ] to [MATH: x_1.] Therefore, [MATH: x_{2}|= x_{1} + 180^{∘}; ≈ 125.54^{∘} + 180^{∘}; = 305.54^{∘}.]

So the solutions, rounded to the nearest degree, are [MATH: x= 126^\circ, 306^\circ.]
